methodology.approach: three-way per-path blob classification (base vs main vs branch), not commit-count or line-count comparison
methodology.classification_rule: for every path that differs between main and branch: ONLY_MAIN_CHANGED if branch's blob == base's blob (branch never touched it); ONLY_BRANCH_CHANGED if main's blob == base's blob; BOTH_CHANGED otherwise (requires manual capability judgment)
methodology.tooling_defect_found_and_fixed: the first implementation used `git rev-parse "$REV:$PATH" 2>/dev/null || echo MISSING`. For a path missing from a tree, `git rev-parse` prints the UNRESOLVED ARGUMENT ITSELF to stdout before exiting non-zero (a documented rev-parse quirk, not present in `git show`/`git cat-file`), so the `||` fallback still ran and both strings concatenated into the captured variable -- producing a unique, non-'MISSING' garbage string per missing path and silently misclassifying every file with a genuinely absent blob on any side as BOTH_CHANGED. Caught by manually re-verifying a handful of already-confirmed-absent paths (e.g. adapter/src/dependency/mod.rs) against the script's own output and finding a contradiction. Fixed by gating on `git cat-file -e` (silent existence check, no stdout) before calling `rev-parse`. This is itself recorded as an instance of this session's own falsification discipline applied to its OWN new tooling, not just to Atlas's semantic extraction.
methodology.corrected_result: 121 total differing paths: 103 ONLY_MAIN_CHANGED, 19 BOTH_CHANGED, 0 ONLY_BRANCH_CHANGED
methodology.significance_of_zero_only_branch_changed: there is not one single file in the entire repository where the branch made an edit that main's independent line left untouched. Main's 127-commit line is a strict superset of the file-level activity surface the branch's 216 commits touched, plus 103 additional paths (mostly whole new files/subsystems) branch never touched at all.
